items.title: Carl Allen interviewed by Monk Rowe, Atlanta, Georgia, January 4, 2013
items.q: I was playing with James Williams and Ray Drummond.

ctx.x: And I just want to, as an aside, you use the word triplet with your students to define the swinging eighth note — the first two notes tied together. Do you verbalize that to them? How would you verbalize that to them?

Well it’s a triple feel versus a duple feel. You know, [scats rhythm] as opposed to [scats]. So that opens up a whole other thing — it can be Latin, straight eighth, funk, R&B, so, a lot of other things. The triplet is hard man. The triplet is hard to deal with. But I think what’s killed the music is not so much the standards. In my opinion it’s more it’s losing its dancability. A great friend a mine, a pianist, said something so hip I wish I had come up with it. And if he wasn’t such a great friend I’d probably…

that it’s about entertainment. It’s not an art form to where, like Christian McBride says all the time he hates it when you play and people look at you like you’re a museum piece while you’re playing. They’re like, hmmm, trying to psychoanalyze it. That’s not what it’s supposed to be. People are supposed to partake in the festivities. People are supposed to enjoy it. Toes are supposed to be tapping. I tell my students all the time, your barometer is look out there, if you don’t see any toes tapping, something’s…
